title: Stocks and flows of natural capital: Implications for Ecological Footprint
evidence_depth: Full six-page article retrieved and extracted; selected passages reviewed
finding_used: Explicit stock-flow agenda; cropland accounting equality and soil depletion omissions; proposed land-type-specific investigation
limits: Not a completed independent account-stock panel or universal stock threshold
design_implication: Foundational prior art; frame study as empirical implementation rather than discovery of stock-flow distinction

title: Accounting for demand and supply of the biosphere’s regenerative capacity: the National Footprint Accounts’ underlying methodology and framework
evidence_depth: Primary full-text selected methods passages, especially sections 3 and 4
finding_used: Biocapacity sums area times yield factor times equivalence factor; cropland production footprint constraints; soil depletion omission
limits: Historical methodology; not verification of every 2026 formula
design_implication: Separate account construction from independent stock measurement; check current vintage

title: Does the Shoe Fit? Real versus Imagined Ecological Footprints
evidence_depth: Primary full-text selected sections including non-carbon components and carbon calculation
finding_used: Critique explicitly identifies accounting balance despite omitted ecosystem harms; distinguishes national trade balance from global overshoot
limits: Perspective; claims and numerical examples refer to historical account editions
design_implication: Do not claim first recognition of ecological masking; distinguish territorial production from consumption

title: The Shoe Fits, but the Footprint is Larger than Earth
finding_used: Defends footprint as demand on regenerative capacity rather than an all-purpose condition measure
limits: Not independent validation of every component or ecological safety
design_implication: Represent the accounting purpose fairly; do not infer stock equivalence from gha

title: Questioning the Ecological Footprint
evidence_depth: Primary abstract and selected introduction/full-text passages
finding_used: Productivity-based accounting and ecological limits are not interchangeable
limits: No independent replication of all debate claims
design_implication: Ground balanced stock-versus-capacity interpretation

title: Towards a 3D National Ecological Footprint Geography
finding_used: Footprint size/depth framework already interprets stock versus flow dependence, applied 1961–2006
limits: Inferred pressure/depth is not direct observation of physical stock trajectories
design_implication: Benchmark against established footprint extensions; avoid claiming first stock-flow footprint diagnostic

title: Tracking national sustainability of critical natural capital and the socioeconomic drivers in the context of the Belt and Road Initiative
evidence_depth: Primary abstract and introduction; title wording should be resolved from DOI before manuscript bibliography
finding_used: Improved 3D EF applied to Belt and Road Initiative countries, 1996–2016; explicitly excludes cross-category deficit compensation and allocates carbon footprint using NPP, following Fang et al. (2018)
limits: Primary abstract/introduction and section snippets, not full methods; stock depletion is inferred within accounting model, not independently observed; BRI means Belt and Road Initiative
design_implication: Acknowledge non-compensation precedents and underlying Fang method; compare independent physical observations, not account-derived depletion against itself

title: Changes in the Fine Composition of Global Forests from 2001 to 2020
evidence_depth: Primary selected full text: results, methods, limitations and data availability
finding_used: Six forest management classes; planted-forest gains offset reported natural-forest area and biomass losses by 59.56% and 77.13%; biomass input at 10 km resampled to 250 m
limits: Resampled biomass is not 250 m independent biomass evidence; no reproduction of authors estimates
design_implication: Closest forest-compensation comparator; demonstrate actual account pairing and validated effective-resolution increment

title: Accounting for forest condition in Europe based on an international statistical standard
evidence_depth: Primary abstract and selected methods/results passages
finding_used: Aggregate European forest-condition improvement coexists with declining condition over about one-third of area
limits: Reference levels, weights and forest types differ; composite condition is not biomass
design_implication: Closely related empirical masking precedent; benchmark reference and aggregation choices

title: System of Environmental-Economic Accounting—Ecosystem Accounting
evidence_depth: Official PDF retrieved through tool; exposed first 30 pages only, selected introductory passages
finding_used: Extent, condition and ecosystem services are distinct accounting objects
limits: Later technical chapters were not reviewed; do not attribute detailed conversion rules to unread chapters
design_implication: Use typed extent/condition/service ledgers and explicit crosswalks; not a new accounting architecture

title: Theoretical and practical issues with measurement of capacity, condition and conversion in the SEEA Ecosystem Accounting
evidence_depth: Primary discussion paper selected passages, including quoted paragraph 4.23
finding_used: Persistent ecosystem conversion and extent-condition boundary are difficult; harvesting can be ambiguous
limits: Discussion/critique paper, not the adopted standard; no independent review of full SEEA chapter 4
design_implication: Validate persistence and destination class; distinguish conversion from temporary disturbance

title: Disentangling the numbers behind agriculture-driven tropical deforestation
finding_used: Agriculture-driven deforestation and subsequent productive agricultural use differ substantially; pasture important
limits: Synthesis, not a forest-to-cropland transition map for the proposed sample
design_implication: Do not equate agricultural drivers with observed cropland conversion; include pasture/other/unknown destinations

title: Intensity analysis to unify measurements of size and stationarity of land changes by interval, category, and transition
finding_used: Established land-change intensity and transition analysis is a relevant comparator
limits: Full text not inspected; does not establish the exact continuous biomass cancellation ratio
design_implication: Treat gross/net and transition analyses as established; resolve detailed methodological overlap if central

title: Global annual cropland dynamics 2015–2024
evidence_depth: Primary selected full text: methods, accuracy table 2, temporal processing and limitations
finding_used: 30 m annual maps; multi-year features/gap filling and isolated-year removal; change accuracy much lower than extent accuracy
limits: Annual label is not independent annual ground truth; study crop definition excludes some vegetation/uses
design_implication: Validate transition classes separately and retain event-year uncertainty; exact title verified via Crossref

title: Annual Croplands dataset, 2015–2024
finding_used: GEE collection projects/glad/Cropland_Annual_2015_2024/YYYY; cropland value 100
limits: No data extraction or license/coverage audit completed
design_implication: Candidate crop layer; archive version, definitions and provenance at data freeze

title: Detecting trends in forest disturbance and recovery using yearly Landsat time series: 1. LandTrendr—Temporal segmentation algorithms
finding_used: Annual trajectory segmentation already detects disturbance and recovery
limits: Algorithm precedent, not validation of biomass or account masking
design_implication: Observed path analysis is established; compare information and errors rather than claim a new path concept

title: Good practices for estimating area and assessing accuracy of land change
finding_used: Probability sampling, area estimation, error matrices and confidence intervals are established change-map practice
limits: No application to proposed sample performed
design_implication: Reference-sample conversion classes; report area-adjusted estimates and uncertainty

title: Using simulation studies to evaluate statistical methods
evidence_depth: Primary selected full text including ADEMP and data-generating mechanisms
finding_used: Aims, data-generating mechanisms, estimands, methods and performance measures; known truth and Monte Carlo uncertainty
limits: General simulation guidance; not ecological calibration evidence
design_implication: Calibrate the whole selected pipeline with nulls and alternative mechanisms; separate simulation operating characteristics from field validation

title: Spatial validation reveals poor predictive performance of large-scale ecological mapping models
finding_used: Spatial dependence can produce optimistic predictive evaluation
limits: Not a universal correction factor or replacement for probability-based map accuracy estimation
design_implication: Use spatially separated evaluation for prediction and avoid train-test leakage

title: Spatial cross-validation is not the right way to evaluate map accuracy
finding_used: Design-based map accuracy differs from model prediction validation
limits: Does not imply random train-test validation solves spatial generalization
design_implication: Separate probability-sample area/accuracy inference from spatial model validation

title: Pervasive shifts in forest dynamics in a changing world
finding_used: Forest demographic change, mortality, growth and recruitment are established subjects
limits: No inventory reanalysis or empirical replenishment threshold derived
design_implication: Demography is a conditional observed-data module, not a new mechanism claim

title: Biomass resilience of Neotropical secondary forests
finding_used: Across 45 Neotropical sites, median recovery to 90% old-growth aboveground biomass estimated at 66 years
limits: Chronosequence inference and region-specific population; not a universal recovery threshold
design_implication: Young-forest gains cannot be assumed immediate replacements for mature forest attributes

title: Multidimensional tropical forest recovery
finding_used: 77 tropical sites and 12 attributes; biomass and species composition recover to 90% on timescales exceeding 12 decades
limits: Different populations/attributes from 2016 study; no global uniform threshold
design_implication: Keep mass, composition and function separate; do not treat different recovery estimates as a contradiction

title: Widespread carbon accumulation in mature forests remains underestimated by satellite observations
finding_used: CONUS mature-forest biomass growth may be missed by satellite estimates
limits: CONUS study, not a global correction; abstract-level evidence only
design_implication: Sensitivity to saturation/underdetection; local validation before extrapolation

title: Accelerating biomass loss from forest disturbances across Europe
finding_used: Reports 6.5 ± 0.8 Pg gross aboveground biomass losses, 1985–2023, 82% associated with harvest
limits: Gross loss is not net stock change; not global; abstract-level evidence only
design_implication: Never relabel mapped local net change as gross harvest or biological turnover

title: Unexpectedly large impact of forest management and grazing on global vegetation biomass
finding_used: Management contributes substantially to difference between actual and potential vegetation biomass
limits: Potential vegetation is counterfactual, not an observed earlier stock
design_implication: Separate reference deficit from observed decline and from causal effect

title: ESA Biomass CCI: Global above-ground biomass maps, v7
finding_used: Published 21 May 2026; 100 m maps for 2005–2012 and 2015–2024; uncertainty and change flags
limits: No raster inspection or accuracy replication
design_implication: Candidate biomass layer; freeze v7 and archive ancillary variables

title: Biomass CCI information for the Global Stocktake
evidence_depth: Official technical guidance page, August 2026 update
finding_used: Annual-average biomass; observation-quality variation; regional biases; independent forest masks and local change validation needed
limits: Provider uncertainty does not establish full correlated change-error model
design_implication: Use appropriate temporal/effective spatial support; validate change; model covariance and bias scenarios

title: SoilGrids documentation / FAQs (candidate screening)
evidence_depth: Search-level screening only; direct fetch returned HTTP 500
finding_used: Global soil product temporal suitability requires explicit checking
limits: FAQ content not directly retrieved; no claim of full documentation review
design_implication: Do not substitute a static or model-based map for repeated soil observations

title: HU-SoilCarbonGrids: An Initiative for Providing Comprehensive Information on Soil Organic Carbon Changes in Hungary
evidence_depth: Primary selected full text: data, modelling and limitations
finding_used: Annual modelled 100 m SOC, 0–30 cm, 1992–2023; 1048 SIMS sites and 9385 observations over 11 epochs 1992–2022; 1992 bulk density/coarse fragments held fixed
limits: Annual predictions are not independent annual measurements; Landsat/climate predictors create shared-input risk and fixed bulk density limits interpretation
design_implication: Hungarian conditional benchmark feasible; test input independence and fixed bulk-density sensitivity

title: GIEMS-MC monthly inundation dataset
finding_used: Monthly 1992–2020 inundation at 0.25 degree
limits: Not fine-scale persistent wetland conversion, nor direct wetland condition
design_implication: Conditional regional hydrologic context, not replacement for validated 30 m conversion

title: RAM Legacy Stock Assessment Database v4.66, assessment-only
evidence_depth: Official archive metadata and file inventory
finding_used: Assessment-only version exists with documented variables and source assessments
limits: No stock series, assessment documents or reference-point histories extracted
design_implication: Candidate fish module only after stock-unit, vintage and biological variable checks

title: Extended RAM Legacy Stock Assessment Database v4.66
evidence_depth: Official archive description and file inventory
finding_used: Extended model-fits version adds conversions and post-hoc modelled reference points; archive recommends assessment-only for typical users
limits: Archive description, not audit of individual assessed stocks
design_implication: Prefer assessment-only; flag supplementation and do not conflate landings with spawning stock biomass

title: Global Forest Resources Assessment 2025: Key findings
evidence_depth: Official key findings, selected extent and stock sections
finding_used: Global forest growing stock, biomass and carbon increased after 2000; tropical declines coexist with boreal/temperate gains; naturally regenerating and primary forest area declined
limits: Country reporting/forest definitions differ from remote sensing; not independent validation of proposed map series
design_implication: Critical counterevidence to presumed global biomass decline; retain concordant as well as divergent cases

citation: Lo et al. / York Ecological Footprint Initiative
title: National Ecological Footprint and Biocapacity Accounts, 2026 Edition: release notes
finding_used: 22 April 2026 release, reported series 1961–2025; built-up GHSL-SMOD, fish and forest trade, ocean sink and country-area revisions affect historical results
limits: Account publication years include estimated years; not all are full-data results
design_implication: Freeze exact 2026 edition and account component; distinguish revised history from physical ecological change

citation: Lin and Wackernagel / Global Footprint Network
title: Estimating the date of Earth Overshoot Day 2026 / Nowcast explained
finding_used: Full UN-based account results cover 1961–2023; 2024–2026 are estimated for the nowcast
limits: Nowcast is not a new independent stock observation
design_implication: 2015–2023 remains a consistent full-account candidate window; do not exclude 2023 using obsolete edition assumptions

title: National Ecological Footprint and Biocapacity Accounts, 2025 Edition: release notes
evidence_depth: Historical official release notes retrieved during screening; exact resolved URL should be rechecked before use
finding_used: Historical edition relevant to vintage comparisons
limits: 2025 release notes were retrieved during screening, but exact PDF locator not retained; landing page is a discovery locator only; superseded by 2026
design_implication: Use only explicit historical-vintage sensitivity, not to set latest full-data cutoff

title: Text recycling guidelines for editors
finding_used: Text recycling differs from redundant publication; justified reuse needs transparency, citation and copyright consideration
limits: Guidance is not individual journal clearance or ethics certification
design_implication: Disclose related internal papers and shared material; show empirical question/data/results increment

title: Drivers of biocapacity and global impact of the world's largest mangrove in ecological footprint accounting
evidence_depth: Primary abstract and selected methods/results, especially sections 2.3–2.9
finding_used: 54 field plots; biomass/stand structure linked to a locally modified biocapacity calculation and spatial reserve/deficit gradients
limits: Cross-sectional; biocapacity partly constructed using biomass inputs, not independent temporal account–stock divergence; published equations require unit scrutiny before reuse
design_implication: Rules out broad first biocapacity–biomass linkage claim; retain independent outcome lineage and do not copy proxy formula

title: Global maps of cropland extent and change show accelerated cropland expansion in the twenty-first century
finding_used: 2003–2019 cropland expansion and NPP increase; 49% of new cropland replaced natural vegetation and tree cover
limits: Broader vegetation/tree-cover class is not all forest; NPP is not stock; article has a 2023 Matters Arising not reviewed here
design_implication: Close observed conversion/productivity precedent; no first expansion-versus-natural-loss claim; inspect linked debate before relying on exact estimates
